title: 1.2 NumPy — the actual foundation
description: This is not "a library." Every tensor operation you will ever write is a NumPy idea wearing a different name.
learningOutcomes: Take every topic in this section to pass 3 of the roadmap's rule: intuition, then derived on paper, then implemented from scratch.

lessons.title: ndarray memory layout: strides, contiguity, views vs copies
learningObjectives: Derive an element address from shape, strides, item size, and an index tuple
Predict whether slicing, reshaping, transposing, and advanced indexing produce a view or a copy
Diagnose non-contiguous arrays and choose deliberately among reshape, ravel, flatten, ascontiguousarray, and copy
Design array boundaries that avoid accidental aliasing and unnecessary materialization
lessons.description: Treat an ndarray as a typed view over a byte buffer, then reason from shape and strides to predict aliasing, contiguity, copies, and performance.

lessons.title: dtype, precision, float32 vs float64 vs bfloat16 — and why it matters for training
learningObjectives: Explain how sign, exponent, and significand bits trade range against precision in common floating formats
Predict NumPy promotion, casting, overflow, underflow, and accumulation behavior at dtype boundaries
Choose storage, compute, and accumulator dtypes for training and inference from measured numerical risk
Build precision checks that use tolerances, stable algorithms, scaling, and finite-value monitoring
lessons.description: Choose numerical representations deliberately by connecting bits to range, precision, promotion, accumulation error, and mixed-precision training behavior.

lessons.title: Broadcasting rules — derive them, don't memorise them
learningObjectives: Derive broadcast compatibility and result shape by aligning operand shapes from the trailing axis
Use singleton axes deliberately to express per-feature, per-example, outer, and batched operations
Explain broadcasting as a zero-stride logical view and predict allocation and performance costs
Diagnose accidental broadcasting, in-place failures, and batch-versus-core dimension mistakes
lessons.description: Derive NumPy broadcasting from trailing-axis alignment, then use explicit singleton dimensions to make vectorized ML code correct, readable, and memory-aware.

lessons.title: Fancy indexing, boolean masking, np.where
learningObjectives: Predict the shape, order, and copy behavior of integer-array and boolean indexing expressions
Choose deliberately among paired coordinate selection, Cartesian products, masks, take, and take_along_axis
Use np.where and ufunc where parameters without computing invalid or needlessly expensive branches
Design validated gather and scatter boundaries that handle repeated indices, memory costs, and semantic axes correctly
lessons.description: Treat advanced indexing as an explicit gather or scatter program, then derive result shape, copy behavior, mask semantics, and conditional selection without relying on trial and error.

lessons.title: Axis semantics — the #1 source of silent bugs in ML code
learningObjectives: Translate between semantic dimension names, positive axes, negative axes, and concrete shape transformations
Design and validate axis contracts for common ML layouts such as NC, NCHW, NHWC, and NTC
Use transpose, moveaxis, swapaxes, expand_dims, squeeze, stack, and concatenate without changing meaning accidentally
Diagnose silent axis bugs with asymmetric fixtures, invariants, and boundary normalization
lessons.description: Make every dimension carry a named meaning, then derive axis-sensitive NumPy code from shape contracts instead of relying on coincidentally equal sizes.

lessons.title: Reductions, keepdims, and why it prevents broadcasting bugs
learningObjectives: Derive reduction output shapes from semantic axes, including tuples of axes and negative axes
Use keepdims to preserve broadcast alignment and prevent same-size dimensions from hiding semantic bugs
Choose accumulator dtype, initial values, masks, and empty-input policy deliberately
Implement and test stable ML reductions such as normalization, softmax, and log-sum-exp
lessons.description: Treat a reduction as a shape transformation with an explicit numerical policy, then preserve reduced axes as singleton dimensions so later broadcasting cannot silently align with the wrong meaning.

lessons.title: einsum — learn it properly, it will make you read papers faster
learningObjectives: Classify labels as output, contracted, batch, or diagonal indices and derive the result shape before executing an einsum
Translate matrix, batched, attention, and paper-style indexed equations into explicit NumPy einsum expressions
Distinguish contraction semantics from broadcasting, diagonal extraction, axis ordering, and ordinary elementwise multiplication
Inspect contraction paths and validate correctness, allocation, and numerical behavior against clearer reference operations
lessons.description: Read einsum as a compact loop-and-reduction specification: derive which indices survive, which are summed, and what each contraction costs before translating paper equations into tested NumPy code.

lessons.title: Linear algebra ops: matmul, solve, inv, svd, eig
learningObjectives: Choose among matmul, solve, least-squares, inverse, SVD, and eigendecomposition from the mathematical question rather than API familiarity
Derive core and batched shapes and validate matrix orientation before calling NumPy linear algebra routines
Diagnose rank deficiency, ill-conditioning, symmetry assumptions, dtype limits, and misleading residual-only checks
Build tested linear algebra boundaries that report numerical evidence and avoid explicit inverses in solve paths
lessons.description: Choose and validate linear algebra operations from the problem being solved, then use conditioning, residuals, rank, and decomposition structure to judge whether a numerical answer deserves trust.

lessons.title: Random number generation and seeding for reproducibility
learningObjectives: Use Generator, BitGenerator, and SeedSequence as separate state, algorithm, and stream-derivation responsibilities
Design reproducible serial and parallel sampling without shared global state or duplicated worker streams
Define what reproducibility promises across reruns, refactors, versions, distributions, and execution order
Test stochastic code through deterministic seams, statistical invariants, state capture, and failure replay
lessons.description: Treat randomness as owned state with an explicit algorithm and stream topology, so experiments can be replayed without coupling every component to one fragile global call order.

lessons.title: Vectorisation: rewriting loops as array ops, and measuring the speedup
learningObjectives: Rewrite element-wise and nested loops as ufunc, broadcasting, reduction, gather, or matrix operations while preserving semantics
Benchmark vectorized alternatives with warm-up, repeated trials, controlled threads, and correctness checks
Identify temporary arrays, memory-bandwidth limits, dtype changes, and cases where chunking or compiled loops beat whole-array vectorization
Report speedup honestly from end-to-end latency, peak memory, and numerical equivalence on representative workloads
lessons.description: Vectorise by identifying array-level operations, then prove the rewrite is worthwhile with representative benchmarks that include correctness, temporary memory, dtype, and end-to-end cost.
